title: Claude Code browser automation: 6 ways compared (2026)
summary: Six ways to give Claude Code a browser, compared: Claude in Chrome, Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, Browser MCP, Browser Use and BrowserOS neo. With setup commands and our own test runs.
body_markdown:
## FAQ


### What is the best browser for Claude Code?


The best browser for Claude Code depends on the job. To test your own app, Playwright MCP needs no logins. To debug a page, Chrome DevTools MCP. For work on sites where you are signed in, use a browser that has your logins: Claude in Chrome, Browser MCP or Browser Use drive your own Chrome, and BrowserOS neo is a separate browser for agents, signed in as you.


### Can Claude Code use my logged-in Chrome?


Yes. Claude in Chrome shares your browser’s login state when you start Claude Code with claude --chrome. Browser MCP and Browser Use also drive your own Chrome profile. Playwright MCP and Chrome DevTools MCP start with a profile of their own unless you connect them to your Chrome.


### Does Claude in Chrome work with an API key?


No. Claude Code’s docs say Chrome integration needs a direct Anthropic plan and a /login sign-in. With an API key, a setup token, Amazon Bedrock or another third-party provider, it stays off. MCP browsers like Playwright MCP and BrowserOS neo work with any Claude Code login.


### Should I use Playwright MCP or Chrome DevTools MCP with Claude Code?


Playwright MCP for driving and testing pages: it reads the accessibility tree and works with Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. Chrome DevTools MCP for debugging: console messages, network requests and performance traces in Chrome.
